meta.title: Asaex — Currency, made effortless
meta.description: A remittance marketplace between licensed exchange offices. Live rates, transparent fees, supervised settlement — usually within one business day.

footer.tagline: Currency, made effortless. You submit a transfer request, a licensed exchange office executes it, and every step runs under platform supervision.
footer.compliance: Asa is a marketplace for remittance between licensed exchange offices. It is not a custodial wallet holding your money, not a securities market, and it holds no deposits.
footer.builtBy: Built by the Â Programming Group

how.title: How a transfer works
how.subtitle: Three clear steps; at each one you know what just happened and what comes next.

1.title: Submit & lock the rate
1.body: Set the amount and destination account; the rate locks for 15 minutes and eligible exchange offices see your request.

2.title: Office accepts, Toman funds
2.body: An office claims the request and chat opens. The Toman leg is funded inside the platform's supervised flow and confirmed by both sides.

3.title: Foreign leg & release
3.body: The office executes the foreign transfer and uploads proof; once receipt is confirmed, the Toman releases and your receipt is issued.

bands.intro: The amount is cut into steps and each step has its own rate. Lower steps are always charged in full, so sending more brings the overall percentage down while never reducing the commission itself.

schedule.splitNote: The platform's share is {pct}% of the commission and the rest goes to the executing office. That split has no effect on what the customer pays.

design.title: The Asaex design system
design.intro: Every token, component, and motion references this page — in both languages and both themes. It is how the three product surfaces (customer PWA, office panel, admin panel) stay coherent.

brand.description: The Asaex mark builds the letter A from two crossing currency flows — reading at once as an A, the exchange arrow-pair (⇄), and flowing water.
brand.markSizes: Legible from a 16px favicon up to a building sign
brand.lockup: Wordmark lockup — in Persian the mark sits on the right
brand.mono: Single-color version for stamps, receipts, and brand surfaces

rules.clearspace: Clear space: the mark's counter height, on all four sides
rules.never: Never: stretch, rotate, add drop shadows, or recolor outside the palette
rules.rtl: Not mirrored in RTL; the lockup order places the mark

colors.description: One deep green accent — trust plus Persian visual heritage, deliberately away from every fintech's blue.
colors.note: Up/down colors are never the only signal; an arrow glyph and an explicit +/− always ride along (a color-vision accessibility requirement).

type.description: Persian in Vazirmatn (1.75 leading), English in Inter (1.6). Display numerals are Persian in fa; inputs and identifiers stay Latin, and every figure is tabular.

layout.description: Spacing only from the 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64 scale; radii 8/12/16/24; exactly three soft elevation levels.

components.description: Interface primitives: buttons, status badges, inputs, and loading skeletons — with touch targets of at least 44px.

validation.description: Validation is real, not cosmetic: Sheba via mod-97, cards via Luhn with BIN→bank lookup, and the national code via its check digit.

err.format: That's not a Sheba format — it starts with IR followed by digits only.
err.length: A Sheba needs exactly 24 digits after IR.
err.checksum: The Sheba check digits don't match — re-check the number.

card.label: Card number
card.hint: 16 digits; the bank is detected from the first six

err.format: A card number is exactly 16 digits.
err.checksum: The card checksum fails — one digit is off.

nid.label: National code
nid.err: Invalid national code — re-check the digits.

coins.description: Twenty currencies, one lighting rig: 45° camera, top-left key light, soft contact shadow, and the currency glyph embossed on the face.
coins.rule: The boundary rule: 3D icons are for currencies and product concepts; functional micro-UI (chevrons, close, search) stays a clean 2px line set — 3D at 16px is noise, not polish.

charts.description: Single series, 2px line, recessive grid, crosshair with tooltip. Value text always wears ink tokens, never the series color; the time axis stays left-to-right in both locales.
charts.note: Direction always pairs an arrow + sign so color is never the only signal.

motion.description: Motion is a product feature here, not decoration: 150–350ms for feedback, 600–1200ms for narrative moments; transform and opacity only.
motion.rules: Under the OS "reduce motion" setting everything collapses to static, and no animation ever blocks interaction or delays a money action.
motion.countdownNote: Below 60s it turns amber and pulses
motion.skeletonNote: Matched to the final layout so layout shift stays at zero

scenes.description: Every scene is built on one rig: the brand-tinted disc, the contact shadow, and the same stroke weight and coin silhouette as the logo and currency icons. SVG + Framer Motion, a few KB each, fully static under the OS reduce-motion setting.

tiles.description: The coin's lighting rig on a rounded square: light from above, a hairline along the top edge, a gloss over the upper half, and a shadow cast in the tile's own colour.
tiles.sizeBody: md beside a list row, lg on a card or a page title, xl alone on an empty screen.
tiles.rule: Colour rule: the hue carries meaning rather than taste — seven cover the whole product, and an eighth means a meaning nobody has named yet. The icon arrives already rendered (icon={<Wallet />}): a lucide component passed as a prop cannot cross from a server component to a client one, and takes the page down with a 500 when it tries.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: What is kept, and for how long.
retention.audit: The audit log (audit_log) is permanent. Rows can be neither edited nor deleted; a database trigger refuses both.
retention.ledger: The ledger (ledger_entries) is permanent, under the same append-only rule. Every figure that moved stays.
retention.kyc: KYC documents live in the private kyc-documents bucket. They are never public and open only through a 60-second signed link.
retention.gap: There is no automatic purge job. Nothing ages out on its own, so a retention window is a decision still to be written down.

balance.zeroBody: In every currency, debits equal credits. That is the only acceptable state for a double-entry ledger.
balance.brokenBody: The difference below is real and needs chasing. It is neither rounded nor hidden; until it reaches zero the reconciliation is not closed.

balance.hint: The ledger's health check: in a correctly kept book, every currency totals exactly zero.

about.title: Seventeen people, spread across the world, on one thing
about.lede: We are a team of seventeen working fully remotely from corners of the world — Tehran and Dubai, Berlin and Toronto. None of us share an office, and all of us work on one thing: making it as simple for an Iranian family to send money as it is to send a message. With love for Iran, and for the Iran being built next.

map.alt: A world map with nine markers, all connected to Tehran, with work moving along the routes between them.
map.caption: Nine points on a map, seventeen people behind it — and one shared route.

product.title: Product design
product.body: Every screen you see was made here: from the transfer flow to a panel an exchange office finishes its work on in four presses.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.body: Our job is to say what this is without overstating it. The number we promise is the number the recipient gets.

bizdev.title: Business development
bizdev.body: We build the network of licensed exchange offices and open the corridors that come next.

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.body: We decide which route opens next, and what we deliberately will not build.

support.title: Support
support.body: When a transfer gets stuck there is a person on the other side who answers — not a bot.

people.title: People
people.body: A team across eight time zones does not hold together on its own. That is somebody's work.

mission.title: Why we do this
mission.body: For many Iranians, sending currency still means trusting an unknown number on Telegram and hoping for the best. We think the same job can be done, with the same real exchange offices, but with a rate you can see, a route you can follow, and a clear answer to who is responsible.

built.title: Built and maintained
built.name: The Â Programming Group
built.body: This product is built and maintained by the Â Programming Group: from the database and the security layer to every screen you see on this site and in the office and admin panels.

contact.title: Something wrong? Tell us.
contact.lede: Write your message and send it. All we need to follow up is a verified phone number — no sign-up, no extra form. Every ticket gets a reference and stays trackable to the end.
contact.subjectPlaceholder: e.g. My Toman payment has not been registered
contact.bodyPlaceholder: The more you write, the faster the answer: order reference, date, amount.

midRate.title: Market base rate
midRate.body: The midpoint between what a currency is being bought and sold for on the open market, right now. It is neither your buying price nor your selling price — it is the middle, and every figure here starts from it so you can check ours against anyone else's.

commission.title: Banded commission
commission.body: The only cost of a transfer. Banded means your amount is cut into slices and each slice has its own rate: the first is charged at 10%, higher ones down to 3%. The more you send, the lower the overall percentage — while the amount of commission never falls by sending more.

commissionCeiling.title: Cost ceiling
commissionCeiling.body: The percentage shown is everything you pay. If an office prices the rate a little away from the base, exactly that much comes off its commission; nothing is added on top of this figure.

rateMarkup.title: Rate difference
rateMarkup.body: Some offices quote a rate slightly above or below the base rate instead of charging a separate fee. It is not an extra cost: it is deducted from the same banded commission.

rateLock.title: Rate lock
rateLock.body: When you open a transfer, the rate is held for you for 15 minutes. Until the countdown ends, whatever the market does has nothing to do with your order. After that you see a fresh rate and confirm again.

refresh.title: Price refresh
refresh.body: Prices update on their own every 30 seconds, and if more than 20 seconds have passed since the last one they are fetched again the moment you come back to the page. The time of the last update is always written beside the price.

identity.title: Identity check
identity.body: Confirming you are who you say: a mobile number, an ID document and a live photo. Anti-money-laundering law requires it for currency transfers, and without it we cannot hand your order to an exchange office.

iban.title: IBAN (Sheba)
iban.body: The 24-character bank account identifier beginning with IR. Its characters carry an arithmetic check, so if you mistype one we tell you here rather than letting money go to the wrong account.

destinationAccount.title: Destination account
destinationAccount.body: The account the money has to arrive in — yours, or the person you are sending to. Saved once, then simply picked next time.

escrow.title: Funds held safely
escrow.body: In a direct trade between two people, the money stays with the platform until both sides have done their part, and is released then. Neither hands over anything without the other.

p2p.title: Peer market
p2p.body: Where people trade directly with each other and the platform is only the safe middle. The two sides set the price themselves, within a permitted band around the market rate.

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.body: The step where money actually moves between accounts. Every settlement has a receipt and is recorded on your order.

twoFactor.title: Two-step sign-in
twoFactor.body: Besides a password, a six-digit code that changes every half minute in an app on your phone. Even somebody who knows your password cannot get in without that phone.

otp.title: One-time code
otp.body: A code sent by text that is valid for a few minutes only. It replaces a fixed password so that there is nothing left to steal.

sla.title: Time commitment
sla.body: What we promise about timing: the same working day as the target, three working days as the contractual maximum. Past that, chasing starts automatically.

corridor.title: Currency route
corridor.body: A pair of source and destination currencies — Toman to Dirham, say. Each route has its own offices and terms.

bubble.title: Coin premium
bubble.body: The gap between a coin's price and the value of the gold inside it. When demand is high the gap widens; the figure shown is that gap.

install.title: Install on your phone
install.body: You can add this to your phone's home screen like an app, without going to an app store. After that it shows the last prices even offline.

openMarket.title: Open market
openMarket.body: The price currencies actually change hands at in free trading, not the central bank's official rate. Every figure in this app is based on it.

pwa.title: Put Asa on your home screen
pwa.body: It opens like an app, starts faster, and shows the last rates even offline.
